catalog_quote: In order to investigate whether it plays a key role in the verbal derivation system, the tone of Shakkinoono is investigated in particular. The researcher used the phonetic analysis program Praat to represent pitch of Shakkinoono. Yet, this pitch representation is not an attempt to give a detailed tone analysis of the language but to give phonetic information about the two contrastive tones of Shakkinoono. Thus, labels such as 'high' and 'low' are used in their relative senses. A phonological tone analysis of this language is needed to give a clearer picture of patterns of tone in Shakkinoono. ... [p.43] Causative verbs are derived in various ways in Shakkinoono as Leslau (1958: 146) observed: "The causative is formed in the following ways: ... by the change of the final -a into -i; and by the change of a stressed syllable into a tone syllable." audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check passes: every quoted string is verbatim at the stated places in the Fufa 2009 text we hold (p.3, p.43) and the held Leslau 1958 Cambridge abstract page (p.135 n.1). (2) The 'tonal' classification itself is safe: three independent statements agree (Leslau 1958 title and French resume 'langue tonale, les tons ayant une valeur phonologique'; Fufa 1996 MA 'Shekacho is a tone language'; Fufa 2009 'two contrastive tones'). sources.note: Syntax/morphology thesis; no phonology chapter. It summarises Leslau 1958 ('The phonology part presents 21 consonant and seven vowel phonemes') and asserts tonality once, fn.7 p.49: 'It is difficult to decide whether the case is nominative or accusative, at this stage. Probably, this case may be manifested in tone since Shekacho is a tone language.' No tone inventory, no tone marking in examples.
